frase_gancho.texto: Tombs with vertical shafts, clay dogs, and hammered copper: the West had its own path.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Western Mexico had no single capital. It was a mosaic of peoples, each with its own ways of living and of burying its dead. The most famous are the shaft tombs: a vertical shaft leading to an underground chamber filled with clay figures. Here you will see the dogs of Colima, warriors in wicker armor, and a couple from Ixtlán del Río. There are also vessels from the Capacha tradition, one of the oldest ceramic traditions in Mexico. You will also find the Purépecha, who worked copper and built yácatas at Tzintzuntzan.
